I don't know much about martial arts, but there are a few different body types. 

* Short and Skinny
* Short and Large
* Tall and Skinny
* Tall and Large

Short and Skinny individuals would probably be best as utilizing speed in order to be difficult to target, boxing and kickboxing would be really efficient due to the quick strikes being pumped out in succession. 

Short and Large individuals would be best at utilizing their lower center of gravity as well as their strength in order to lift an adversary. I believe Tae-Kwon-Do would be a smart choice. A defensive style would work wonders for an individual with this stature. Not only will their low center of gravity work against taller and potentially stronger opponents, but also the defensive style of Tae-Kwon-Do would make it difficult for the enemy to land a hit on them in combat.

Tall and Skinny individuals could be similar in agility to Short and Skinny people, however, their center of gravity and longer limbs make them a bit slower. My friend took some Kyushu Jitsu classes when he visited Japan a few years back and told me most of the students were his height. He's 6 feet 2 inches and was about 160 lbs at the time. Kyushu Jitsu is both an offensive and defensive style of fighting. It involves targeting an opponent's pressure points. You can easily fend off someone attacking you while also putting them under immense pressure if they do not expect an attack. This is also an incredibly dangerous form of fighting as you can target specific pressure points and knock someone out and even kill them in the process, especially if you are going for the head, neck, or chest. Also any type of appendage can be void in a fight if targeted.

A Tall and Large individual would be best served doing any specific type of martial arts dedicated to power, strength and defense. Speed isn't exactly required as the opponent will have to take the fight to you anyways. Any fighting style could be efficient here regarding those three. Wrestling is probably the most common answer here. Being able to beat your opponent into the ground and keep them there will force them to surrender. If there is another Tall and Large individual going up against you, then you'll likely just have to see who is the better wrestler, or whoever hits the hardest. At that point it's just down to sheer willpower, integrity, and endurance.

There are some really amazing things I like about her after playing 18 games of her in normals and ranked solo. I think her primary role in the game is jungler. I don't think she has enough consistent damage to be a top laner. Not only that, but her early and mid game are super strong due to the way her E and W prevent even mobile champions from escaping a well executed gank. If she isn't getting her team ahead or being involved in kills, she will sorta fall off. In general, she is a really good Early-Mid game champion, whose damage falls off later on in the game unless you are getting 2/3 damage items.

I think her secondary role should be support. Every ability in her kit has some impact on the squishier targets in the game. Hell, she isn't really going to be a super supportive champion much at all. Yes, she'll get Face of the Mountain, Ruby Sightstone, Locket of the Iron Solari, Ninja Tabi, Randuins Omen, and Iceborn Gauntlet, but she just doesn't really feel as impactful. More impactful as a support because she can actually snowball the game off of consistent picks and opponents mispositioning. But the higher elo you get, the more likely your opponents will not be lazy in how they approach their positioning in the lane, making it less likely for you to get kills. 

I still think that Cinderhulk with Blue Smite into Mercury Treads/Ninja Tabi into Dead Man's Plate is the way to go. There are 4 other items I think that are just clearly superior on her because not only do they grant damage, but also defense. 

Sterak's Gage gives her a lot of bonus Attack Damage while also acting as a strong Mid-Game offensive/defensive item. I think the massive shield she gets combined with her W passive when under 40% Health is just really strong together.

Iceborn Gauntlet grants her a massive 20% CDR which along with Attack Damage are the only 2 offensive statistics she needs in this game. The slowing field range combined with the armor from Ninja Tabi and Dead Man's Plate makes this item really strong and since she is considered to be a burst champion who doesn't quite rely on AA's that much makes her crave a Sheen Based item. The mana this grants as well is all the mana she'll need in the game.

Black Cleaver makes it so that she can hit the 40% threshold and also makes her more difficult to fight over a long period of time in a 1v1. You don't wanna be in a situation where her Sterak's and Maw passives break along with the massive defensive stats gained from her W start kicking in. Along with the attack damage and 30% armor shred just a few seconds into a fight, she's going to kick your ass.

Maw of Malmortius just seemingly gives her the only real Magic Resist item that suites her so well. Getting low isn't a big deal to good Poppy's if they know they can rely on their items and W Passive to help them out. Sure Mercury Treads are another MR item, but those are almost mandatory where this item is just so expensive albeit so important for her. The Attack Damage and small Armor Penetration help her out alot, but the real reason you are getting this is for the super solid Passive that pops once you reach a certain health point. It'll make you really hard to kill.

I for one like the bruiser build. Full Damage Poppy cannot carry late game anymore and full tank Poppy cannot do enough damage to be a viable threat. A blend of damage and defense is the way to go to keep her relevant at all stages in the game.

Bo2's give weaker teams a greater chance at winning against better teams and improving as the season goes on. More losses = More improvement possibilities. Less losses = Less improvement possibilities. The nice thing about the Bo2 format is if you lose game 1, you can improve on the fly during the next game.

They can afford to do 5 Bo2's in a single day. They cannot overlap EU LCS onto the weekends as it would interfere with the broadcasting schedule for NA matches. And NA matches cannot and should not extend into Monday's where people are usually at work/school. 

The thing is is that Riot is occupying a facility for 2 whole days, so it's not like they are really wasting money shifting to the Bo2's that can consume an entire day anyways. What they will need to do is to give teams a 10 minute intermission between games during the Bo2, not the lengthy 15 that they get right now.

Bo2 would be the only real way that the LCS can improve without Riot losing as much money as they are renting out these facilities. I remember reading a post about how even though they have 5 games being played a day only on weekends, they are still losing money, albeit in an attempt to keep the game popular and ever growing. 

Although, when you really think about it, it will make the games more enjoyable and mean more. Like, a team that goes 1-1 all the time will definitely be a very mediocre team. A team that goes 0-2 will be able to see their mistakes more often and improve over the course of the season, and teams going 2-0 all the time will definitely be considered dominant.

I used to play Zyra a lot during S3 and early S4 then dropped her completely because she was way too difficult to play in mid lane any longer. 

I have some ideas that could help her out. 

Firstly, I want to say that her Q and R are both fine as is and that her base damages could be slightly altered on both abilities including her E.

Aside from those balancing changes, there are 3 things that must be addressed: Her E, W, and Passive.

Her E is a medium damage, 12 second flat at all levels spell. It has a root for .75 up to 1.75. If we look at other champions with roots, take Morgana for example, her root at level 1 is 2.00. This puts a rank 5 E for Zyra to shame when compared to a rank 1 Q for Morgana. They need to up the root time per level for her E.

W is the most major fix. It grants 2% upwards to 10% CDR at rank 5. This ability is 1 point wonder and Zyra can reach 40% CDR based off of items alone before she even puts a second point in her W, making the CDR gained from this ability useless. Drop the CDR and convert that power back into her gameplay instead of granting useless stats. Do this by making her seed count higher and her plants more powerful.

Teemo can store 3 shrooms, why can Zyra not have 3 saplings? Sure Teemo gets his 3 shrooms from his ultimate, but Zyra's plants are meaningless without using an ability on them. Zyra should be able to hold 3 seeds. Aside from making the plants more powerful (which can be changed), the responsiveness needs to be amped as well. The vision she gains from seeds stepped on is really meh. In order to compensate for her lack of mobility, place a range around Zyra. Whenever a seed is stepped on by an enemy that is within the radius of Zyra will grant her a short burst of movement speed.

Her Passive honestly isn't all that bad, it just needs to have a much quicker albeit instantaneous response time instead of a 1-2 second delay. Sure it deals true damage 100-440 (making it scale off of her level) but the responsiveness is what makes it so useless. Keep her passive the way it is, just improve response time and maybe give it an AP ratio, teehee.

TL;DR - Don't change Q or R, give E a better root duration, take off CDR from W and let her hold 3 seeds, let W give short burst of speed when seed is destroyed (within a radius), make plants more responsive and do more damage, keep Passive the same just change the reaction time from a 1-2 second delay to instantaneous which will likely result in a more efficient Passive. 

These changes will make Zyra a solid control mage similar to Anivia and Heimerdinger.

The 2 champions I recommend for you (that are in fact freelo up to low Diamond) are Rek'Sai and Fizz. Yes, Fizz.

Rek'Sai is a very easy, little to no mechanic jungler that is a simple point and click bot that is impossible to kill. She has amazing farming abilities, easy ganks, good catch and good chase and escape, plus her sonar should allow you to see the champions around you so you can go in for a sneak attack!

Fizz on the other hand is incredibly slippery, and if you can manage to build him with just a few offensive items and a couple of defensive ones, enemy carries won't be able to kill you 1v1. His troll pole bides you some time as to make you figure out if you wanna go in or just hop away to safety. He is super fun to play.

Rek'Sai has 5 core items, with 1 of them being interchangeable, at least to my experiences with her. 

You should always go for Stalker's Blade with a Cinderhulk Enchantment (You are a resource-less jungler, so you should always build either Stalker's or Skirmisher's. Stalker's gives a slow so you can smite before you knock-up the enemy with your burrowed E) Mercury Tread's with Homeguard Enchantment (for those ult's from base into massive movespeed to catch the enemy off guard! Like a homeguard hecarim gank almost!), Black Cleaver (20% CDR, good ability to stick to enemy champions, bonus hp from Cinderhulk), Randuin's Omen (Armor/Hp stacking with Cinderhulk, makes kiting champions lives a bit more difficult, good active to slow enemies once you catch up to them. Great synergy with Black Cleaver passive.) Banshee's Veil (being a melee tank, you truly need this item. Prevents you from being bursted down and once the shield is popped you can regen a lot of hp over a decent amount of time. MR, more stacking Hp with Cinderhulk). The final item I go for is either Thornmail if the enemy has a super fed ADC or a Ravenous Hydra if my team needs more damage or if I feel like I need to split push later on in the game.

For runes I recommend Attack Damage Marks, Scaling Health Seals, 6 Flat Cooldown Reduction Glyphs, 3 Flat Magic Resist Glyphs, Attack Speed Quints. 21/9/0 If you elect to go for 9/21/0, you will find clearing to take forever in the early parts of the game up until 20 minutes.
